governance.claim_status: All additions are public-source candidate records; none are claimed participants.
governance.living_map_rule: PROVISIONAL means candidate geography/entity identity still requires LM canonical-location resolution before publication.

records.name: Apirana Bush Regeneration Group
records.relationship: Restores native vegetation in Apirana Reserve and contributes to the ecological health of the Ōmaru Stream headwaters.
records.summary: Community volunteers undertake weed control, native forest regeneration and riparian restoration in the southern section of Apirana Reserve.
records.detail: The group combines ongoing volunteer work with professional ecological support to reduce weed competition, establish native forest and improve water quality in the Ōmaru Stream catchment.

records.name: Birkenhead War Memorial Park Volunteers
records.relationship: Volunteer stewardship group working within Birkenhead War Memorial Park.
records.summary: Local volunteers support ecological restoration and biodiversity protection in and around Birkenhead War Memorial Park.
records.detail: Auckland's conservation directory records the group as active in pest animal and plant control, planting and habitat restoration, and species management and monitoring.

records.name: Mahurangi West Pest Group
records.relationship: Supports community-led pest control in the Mahurangi West landscape.
records.summary: A local conservation group focused on reducing ecological pressure from introduced pests and supporting native biodiversity around Mahurangi West.
records.detail: The group forms part of the wider Restore Rodney East network of community conservation projects operating across north-eastern Auckland.

records.name: Eastern Bays Songbird Project
records.relationship: A 4,000-hectare urban ecological network linking communities across Auckland's eastern suburbs.
records.summary: Mobilises residents and organisations to restore natural ecosystems and create an urban sanctuary in which native birds and invertebrates can flourish.
records.detail: The project coordinates community trapping and ecological restoration across its multi-suburb project area and contributes to Pest Free Auckland 2050 and Predator Free NZ 2050.

records.name: Takatu Wetland Restoration Group
records.relationship: Restores the ecologically significant Takatu Wetland.
records.summary: Community conservation group working to restore Takatu Wetland, which Auckland Council lists as a significant ecological area.
records.detail: Initial restoration work targets invasive spiky rush that contributes to waterway silting, followed by planting intended to reduce runoff from surrounding pasture.

records.name: Leigh Penguin Project
records.relationship: Community conservation initiative associated with protection of penguins and their coastal habitat around Leigh.
records.summary: Local project contributing to seabird awareness and conservation in the Leigh coastal environment.
records.detail: Included in the Restore Rodney East network; profile detail should remain candidate-level until the group supplies or confirms further information.

records.name: Jaggers Bush Restoration Group
records.relationship: Restores a significant coastal broadleaf forest remnant between Westmere and Seddon Fields.
records.summary: Local residents run predator-control and community weed-control work to strengthen native habitat in Jaggers Bush.
records.detail: The group supplements Auckland Council predator control with an approved trapline and community weeding, helping native seedlings regenerate in a Significant Ecological Area.

records.name: Te Korowai o Waiheke
records.relationship: Island-scale biodiversity initiative supporting a predator-free Waiheke.
records.summary: Coordinates and supports community predator-control activity across Waiheke, working with neighbourhood groups and conservation partners.
records.detail: Te Korowai o Waiheke connects local trapping groups and island-wide conservation action, building community participation in the protection and recovery of Waiheke's native biodiversity.

records.name: Awhitu Peninsula Landcare Incorporated
records.relationship: Community-led restoration across the 22,000-hectare Āwhitu Peninsula.
records.summary: Works with landowners, volunteers and partners to restore waterways, wetlands, indigenous vegetation and wildlife corridors while reducing pest animals and plants.
records.detail: Established in 1994, Āwhitu Landcare operates across the peninsula and has produced and planted hundreds of thousands of eco-sourced native plants while expanding pest-management and biodiversity work.

records.name: Pest Free Piha
records.relationship: Community-led programme working to restore biodiversity across Piha village and catchment.
records.summary: Brings neighbourhood efforts together to control pest animals and invasive plants and protect Piha's native ecosystems.
records.detail: The initiative supports integrated pest management, weed replacement with locally sourced natives, kauri-dieback protection and coordinated volunteer action across the Piha catchment.

records.name: Matuku Reserve
records.relationship: Protected native wetland and forest habitat within the wider Te Henga ecological landscape.
records.summary: Forms part of a connected conservation landscape alongside Matuku Link and other Te Henga restoration projects.
records.detail: The reserve adjoins Matuku Link, whose restoration and predator-control work helps create a connected corridor for rare wetland and forest species in the Waitākere River Valley.

records.name: Ōmaha Shorebird Sanctuary
records.relationship: Community stewardship of important shorebird habitat at Ōmaha.
records.summary: Supports protection of coastal nesting and roosting habitat and raises community awareness of vulnerable shorebirds.
records.detail: The sanctuary is part of the wider network of community conservation initiatives operating around Rodney's eastern coastline.

records.name: Rocky Bay Rat Busters
records.relationship: Neighbourhood trapping group contributing to predator control on Waiheke.
records.summary: Mobilises residents around Rocky Bay / Ōmiha to control rodents and strengthen native biodiversity.
records.detail: The group is listed by Te Korowai o Waiheke among active Waiheke community groups controlling rodents and seeking volunteer participation.

records.name: Mahurangi East Land Restoration
records.relationship: Community ecological restoration activity in the Mahurangi East landscape.
records.summary: Supports local habitat restoration and biodiversity improvement around Mahurangi East and Snells Beach.
records.detail: Included within the Restore Rodney East network; detailed project claims should be confirmed with the organisation before a claimed profile is published.

records.name: Pupuke Birdsong Project
records.relationship: A community environmental hub connecting restoration work across Takapuna North.
records.summary: Engages residents, schools and organisations in tree planting, predator and pest-plant control, water-quality improvement and community-led environmental projects.
records.detail: The project spans the Takapuna North area from Sunnynook to Hauraki Corner and provides practical support and pest-control equipment while coordinating volunteer environmental action.

records.name: Hauraki Gulf Conservation Trust
records.relationship: Initiates and supports conservation and environmental projects across Tīkapa Moana / the Hauraki Gulf.
records.summary: Supports restoration, research, conservation funding and community environmental projects, with a long record of activity on Waiheke and other Gulf islands.
records.detail: Established in 1997, the Trust has supported projects including wetland restoration, pest eradication, environmental education and island restoration, and helps other groups with conservation funding.

records.name: Ark in the Park Buffer Zone
records.relationship: Supports the ecological protection surrounding Ark in the Park in the Waitākere Ranges.
records.summary: Extends community conservation and pest-control pressure around the open sanctuary landscape.
records.detail: Ark in the Park is an 1,843-hectare conservation partnership protecting remnant kauri forest and threatened native species; the buffer relationship helps reduce reinvasion pressure around that core project.

records.name: Friends of Maungawhau
records.relationship: Candidate environmental/community relationship associated with Maungawhau / Mount Eden.
records.summary: The current candidate requires identity disambiguation before ecological claims are published, because web search also returns a school community group using the same name.
records.detail: Retained as a candidate but deliberately not over-enriched: the name is ambiguous in public search results and should be resolved before profile publication.

records.name: BirdCare Aotearoa
records.relationship: Auckland-based native bird hospital supporting wildlife recovery across the wider region.
records.summary: Provides clinical care and rehabilitation for sick, injured and orphaned native birds and supports the public and conservation organisations with rescue advice and training.
records.detail: BirdCare Aotearoa operates from Green Bay and is DOC-permitted to rehabilitate native, endangered and at-risk wild birds, working with rescuers, councils, conservation organisations and veterinary partners.

records.name: Restoration Ruatuna
records.relationship: Restores and protects the native environment of the Ruatuna catchment at Laingholm.
records.summary: Local volunteers remove weeds, restore public spaces, control predators, monitor stream health and engage neighbours in catchment restoration.
records.detail: Active since 2018, the group works across the Ruatuna valley, ridges, stream and beach and operates a community trap library. Research corrected the seed locality from Titirangi to Laingholm.

records.name: Pest Free Matakana
records.relationship: Community pest-control initiative supporting biodiversity around Matakana.
records.summary: Engages local people in reducing introduced predators and improving habitat conditions for native wildlife.
records.detail: Part of the Restore Rodney East conservation network. Detailed operational claims remain candidate-level pending direct profile confirmation.

records.name: Te Waipuna Puāwai Trust
records.relationship: Community-based environmental activity associated with Ranui and western Auckland.
records.summary: Supports local environmental restoration and community engagement, including work around waterways and ecological education.
records.detail: The candidate is retained from the Auckland conservation network; further direct-source research is recommended before adding more specific claims.

records.name: Titirangi Urban Sanctuary
records.relationship: Neighbourhood-scale conservation supporting native biodiversity in Titirangi.
records.summary: Connects household and community action with pest control and ecological restoration in the Waitākere foothills.
records.detail: The initiative sits within the wider Pest Free Waitākere Ranges community network. Detailed profile information should be confirmed directly before claim verification.

records.name: Sustainable Papakura
records.relationship: Works with the Papakura community to build practical, environmentally sustainable ways of living.
records.summary: Provides workshops, activities and community opportunities that help people grow, make, repair and adopt lifestyles that better support Papatūānuku.
records.detail: Sustainable Papakura focuses on a vibrant, connected and eco-friendly community, working with individuals, families, groups and organisations to build practical sustainability skills.

records.name: Predator Free Swanson / Waitākere
records.relationship: Community-powered predator control across Swanson and Waitākere.
records.summary: Supports residents with trapping knowledge, equipment guidance and shared monitoring to reduce rats, possums and mustelids and protect native wildlife.
records.detail: The group promotes coordinated backyard and landscape trapping, catch recording and community participation to improve ecosystem health and breeding prospects for native birds and other fauna.
